Community Endorsements

Our Community Stands Together

Neighbors from every walk of life — teachers, business owners, parents, retirees, faith leaders — are united in support of Measure L. Here's why.

Featured Voice

"I've volunteered here for twelve years. I've watched this library become a lifeline — for the single mother who needs job search help, for the elderly man who just wants a warm place to read, for the child who lights up when she finds her first chapter book. Vote yes. This is not the time to let them down."

DV
Dolores Vargas President, Friends of the Library — Retired Nurse, 28-year Evergreen resident
347

Community members have signed in support

Educators & School Staff

What our educators say

MC

"My students use the library every week. The homework help program has been a lifeline for families who can't afford tutors. Cutting those hours means some kids simply don't get help. We cannot afford to lose this."

Margaret Chen

3rd Grade Teacher, Lincoln Elementary School

TK

"The summer reading program is one of the most impactful things we can offer kids whose families can't afford camps or enrichment. It's free, it's joyful, and it prevents the learning loss we fight against every September."

Thomas Kwon

Principal, Evergreen Middle School

RP

"The library is where the school day continues after the bell rings. It's where a kid with no quiet place at home can actually concentrate. Measure L is a vote for every student in this town."

Rita Patel

School Librarian; Teachers' Union Local 445 Rep.

Parents & Families

SK

"My daughter learned to read with the summer reading program. My son found his passion for science through library workshops. These programs aren't extras — they're how kids stay sharp and families stay connected."

Sarah Kim

Parent; Westside PTA President

MO

"We moved here two years ago and didn't know anyone. The library's family programs introduced us to other parents. Now it's our community center. Losing Sunday hours would mean losing our Sunday routine."

Mei-Ling Osei

Parent of three; new Evergreen resident

BT

"As a single dad working two jobs, the library's free after-school homework help program is not optional for us. It's the difference between my kids doing well in school or falling behind. $3.20 a month is an easy yes."

Bernard Torres

Father of two; Essential services worker

Business & Civic Leaders

RO

"A strong community needs a strong library. My customers talk about this place like it's the heart of the neighborhood. Measure L is good for business, good for families, and good for Evergreen. I'm voting yes."

Robert Okafor

Owner, Okafor Hardware — Main Street, 32 years

JW

"Every Sunday we'd see library visitors stop in for coffee after their morning reading. Closing Sundays doesn't just hurt the library — it changes the whole feel of the neighborhood. Measure L protects what makes Evergreen special."

"Our library serves everyone who walks through its doors — regardless of income, age, or background. It embodies our community's best values. Please vote yes on June 18."
